_readme: HOW TO EDIT THIS FILE (JSON does not allow comments, so the notes live here).
To add a question: copy one object inside a chapter's 'questions' list, then change its text.
'options' must contain exactly 4 texts. 'answer' is the letter of the correct option: A, B, C or D.
'difficulty' must be one of: easy, medium, hard. Keep a mix so short quizzes stay balanced.
'id' must be unique. 'topic' is optional but used for the 'topics to revise' list on the results page.
To activate another chapter: replace its 'Title not added yet' with the official title, add 'description', 'topics', and questions, then set 'available' to true.
A chapter is shown as available only when 'available' is true AND it has at least one valid question.
Remember: do not leave a trailing comma after the last item of a list, and keep the file saved as UTF-8.
subject: Chemistry

chapters.title: Chemical Equilibrium
chapters.description: Reversible reactions, dynamic equilibrium, the law of mass action, equilibrium constants and the reaction quotient.
topics: Basic equilibrium concepts (reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium)
Predicting the direction of a reaction

questions.question: What is a reversible reaction?
options: A reaction that proceeds in the forward direction only
A reaction that can proceed in both the forward and the backward direction
A reaction that takes place only in the presence of a catalyst
A reaction that stops after a short time
questions.explanation: In a reversible reaction the products can react with each other to form the reactants again, so the reaction goes both ways.

questions.question: Which symbol is used to represent a reversible reaction?
questions.explanation: The double arrow ⇌ shows that the forward and the reverse reactions occur at the same time.

questions.question: Which of the following is a reversible reaction?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen and iodine form hydrogen iodide, and HI also decomposes back into H₂ and I₂, so the reaction is reversible.

questions.question: At chemical equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction is ______ the rate of the reverse reaction.
questions.explanation: Equilibrium is reached when the forward and reverse rates become equal.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an irreversible reaction?
questions.explanation: Burning of magnesium goes to completion; the magnesium oxide does not change back into magnesium and oxygen under ordinary conditions.

questions.question: Why is chemical equilibrium called a dynamic equilibrium?
options: Because both the forward and reverse reactions keep taking place at equal rates
Because only the forward reaction continues
questions.explanation: Nothing seems to change at equilibrium, but molecules keep reacting in both directions at the same rate.

questions.question: At equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants and products:
questions.explanation: Because the forward and reverse rates are equal, the amounts of reactants and products stay constant. They need not be equal to each other.

questions.question: What is meant by active mass?
options: The total mass of a substance in grams
The atomic mass of an element
The molar concentration of a substance, in mol dm⁻³
The volume of the reaction vessel
questions.explanation: Active mass is the concentration of a substance expressed in moles per dm³.

questions.question: How is the molar concentration of a substance A written?
questions.explanation: Square brackets around the formula, such as [A], stand for the molar concentration.

questions.question: Who proposed the law of mass action?
questions.explanation: The law of mass action was put forward by the Norwegian chemists Cato Guldberg and Peter Waage in 1864.

questions.question: According to the law of mass action, the rate of a chemical reaction is directly proportional to:
options: The mass of the products only
The temperature of the surroundings only
The volume of the container only
The product of the active masses of the reactants
questions.explanation: Rate ∝ product of the active masses (concentrations) of the reacting substances, each raised to the power of its coefficient.

questions.question: What does the subscript 'c' in Kc stand for?
questions.explanation: Kc is the equilibrium constant expressed in terms of molar concentrations.

questions.question: What is the correct expression of Kc for N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃?
questions.explanation: Products go in the numerator and reactants in the denominator. Each concentration is raised to the power of its coefficient: 2 for NH₃, 1 for N₂ and 3 for H₂.

questions.question: A very large value of Kc (much greater than 1) shows that at equilibrium:
options: Reactants are present in much larger amounts than products
Products are present in much larger amounts than reactants
questions.explanation: Kc = [products] / [reactants]. A large Kc means the numerator is large, so the equilibrium mixture is rich in products.

questions.question: A very small value of Kc (much less than 1) shows that at equilibrium:
options: Products are present in much larger amounts than reactants
Reactants are present in much larger amounts than products
questions.explanation: A small Kc means the numerator (products) is small compared with the denominator (reactants).

questions.question: A reversible reaction can reach a state of chemical equilibrium only in:
options: A system with a catalyst only
questions.explanation: In an open system the substances can escape, so the forward and reverse reactions cannot balance. Equilibrium needs a closed system.

questions.question: In the Kc expression, the concentrations of the products are written in the:
questions.explanation: Kc = [products] / [reactants], so products form the numerator.

questions.question: The reaction quotient is represented by the symbol:
questions.explanation: Qc is the reaction quotient. It has the same form as Kc but is calculated at any stage of the reaction.

questions.question: What is the Kc expression for 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃?
questions.explanation: Product SO₃ has coefficient 2; SO₂ has coefficient 2 and O₂ has coefficient 1. So Kc = [SO₃]² / ([SO₂]²[O₂]).

questions.question: What is the Kc expression for N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂?
questions.explanation: NO₂ is the product with coefficient 2, so it is squared in the numerator. N₂O₄ is the reactant with coefficient 1.

questions.question: What is the unit of Kc for N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃?
questions.explanation: Kc = (mol dm⁻³)² / [(mol dm⁻³)(mol dm⁻³)³] = (mol dm⁻³)⁻² = dm⁶ mol⁻².

questions.question: What is the unit of Kc for PCl₅ ⇌ PCl₃ + Cl₂?
questions.explanation: Kc = (mol dm⁻³)(mol dm⁻³) / (mol dm⁻³) = mol dm⁻³.

questions.question: Kc of which of the following reactions has no unit?
questions.explanation: In N₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2NO the total number of moles is 2 on each side, so the units cancel completely.

questions.question: For H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI, the equilibrium concentrations are [H₂] = 0.1, [I₂] = 0.2 and [HI] = 0.6 mol dm⁻³. What is Kc?
The reaction quotient Qc is calculated using the concentrations present:
options: Only when the reaction is at equilibrium
At any given moment during the reaction
questions.explanation: Qc has the same expression as Kc, but it can be worked out for any mixture, whether or not it is at equilibrium.

questions.question: If Qc is less than Kc, the reaction will proceed:
options: In the reverse direction, towards reactants
In the forward direction, towards products
In neither direction, because it is at equilibrium
Only after a catalyst is added
questions.explanation: Qc < Kc means there are too many reactants compared with equilibrium, so the net reaction shifts forward to form more products.

questions.question: If Qc is equal to Kc, the reaction mixture is:
questions.explanation: When Qc = Kc, the concentrations are the equilibrium concentrations and there is no net change.

questions.question: For a certain reaction Kc = 4 at a given temperature. What is the value of Kc for the reverse reaction at the same temperature?
questions.explanation: The Kc of the reverse reaction is the reciprocal of the forward Kc: 1 / 4 = 0.25.

questions.question: The value of Kc for a given reaction depends on:
options: The initial concentrations of the reactants
The time allowed for the reaction
questions.explanation: For a given reaction, Kc changes only when the temperature changes.

questions.question: What is the effect of a catalyst on a reversible reaction?
options: It increases the value of Kc
It helps equilibrium to be reached faster without changing the value of Kc
It decreases the value of Kc
It converts the reaction into an irreversible reaction
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached sooner but Kc is not changed.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true for a system at chemical equilibrium?
options: The rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal
Both the forward and reverse reactions have stopped
Observable properties such as colour remain constant
The concentrations of reactants and products stay constant
questions.explanation: Equilibrium is dynamic: the reactions do not stop, they continue at equal rates.

questions.question: In terms of rate constants, the equilibrium constant Kc is equal to:
options: kf / kr (forward rate constant divided by reverse rate constant)
questions.explanation: At equilibrium kf[reactants] = kr[products], so [products] / [reactants] = kf / kr = Kc.

questions.question: For the reaction 2A + B ⇌ C + D, the rate of the forward reaction according to the law of mass action is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Each active mass is raised to the power of its coefficient, so rate ∝ [A]² [B]. The product concentrations [C][D] belong to the reverse reaction.

questions.question: In the Kc expression, the power to which each concentration is raised is equal to:
options: Its coefficient in the balanced chemical equation
questions.explanation: The balanced equation's coefficients become the exponents of the concentrations in Kc.

questions.question: A reaction has a Kc value close to 1. At equilibrium, the mixture contains:
options: Appreciable amounts of both reactants and products
questions.explanation: Kc ≈ 1 means that the concentrations of products and reactants are of comparable size.

questions.question: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ at equilibrium, [N₂] = 0.2, [H₂] = 0.1 and [NH₃] = 0.4 mol dm⁻³. Calculate Kc.
For PCl₅ ⇌ PCl₃ + Cl₂ at equilibrium, [PCl₃] = 0.3, [Cl₂] = 0.3 and [PCl₅] = 0.15 mol dm⁻³. Calculate Kc.
For H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI, Kc = 49 at a certain temperature. If [H₂] = [I₂] = 0.1 mol dm⁻³ at equilibrium, what is [HI]?
For N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂, Kc = 4.0 mol dm⁻³ at a certain temperature. A mixture has [N₂O₄] = 0.5 and [NO₂] = 1.0 mol dm⁻³. What happens?
options: Qc = 2.0, so the reaction proceeds in the forward direction
Qc = 2.0, so the reaction proceeds in the reverse direction
Qc = 0.5, so the reaction proceeds in the forward direction
Qc = 4.0, so the mixture is at equilibrium
questions.explanation: Qc = [NO₂]² / [N₂O₄] = (1.0)² / 0.5 = 2.0. Since Qc (2.0) < Kc (4.0), the net reaction goes forward to make more NO₂.

questions.question: For A + B ⇌ C + D, Kc = 10. A mixture has [A] = 0.1, [B] = 0.2, [C] = 0.5 and [D] = 0.4 mol dm⁻³. What can be concluded?
options: The reaction will go forward because Qc < Kc
The reaction will go in reverse because Qc > Kc
The mixture is at equilibrium because Qc = Kc = 10
Nothing can be predicted without a catalyst

questions.question: For H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI, Kc = 50. A mixture contains [H₂] = 0.1, [I₂] = 0.1 and [HI] = 1.0 mol dm⁻³. Which statement is correct?
options: Qc = 100, so more HI forms (forward direction)
Qc = 10, so more HI forms (forward direction)
Qc = 50, so the mixture is at equilibrium
questions.explanation: Qc = [HI]² / ([H₂][I₂]) = (1.0)² / (0.1 × 0.1) = 100. Since Qc > Kc, there is too much product and the reaction proceeds in reverse.

questions.question: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, Kc = 800 at a certain temperature. What is Kc for 2NH₃ ⇌ N₂ + 3H₂ at the same temperature?
questions.explanation: Reversing the reaction inverts the equilibrium constant: 1 / 800 = 1.25 × 10⁻³.

questions.question: At equilibrium, a 2 dm³ vessel contains 0.5 mol PCl₅, 0.6 mol PCl₃ and 0.6 mol Cl₂. What is Kc for PCl₅ ⇌ PCl₃ + Cl₂?
questions.explanation: Convert moles to concentration first: PCl₅ = 0.25, PCl₃ = 0.30, Cl₂ = 0.30 mol dm⁻³. Kc = (0.30 × 0.30) / 0.25 = 0.36 mol dm⁻³.

questions.question: 1.0 mol of H₂ and 1.0 mol of I₂ are placed in a 1 dm³ vessel. At equilibrium, 1.6 mol of HI is present. What is Kc for H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI?
questions.explanation: 1.6 mol HI needs 0.8 mol each of H₂ and I₂, leaving 0.2 mol dm⁻³ of each. Kc = (1.6)² / (0.2 × 0.2) = 2.56 / 0.04 = 64.

questions.question: What is the unit of Kc for 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃?
questions.explanation: Kc = (mol dm⁻³)² / [(mol dm⁻³)² (mol dm⁻³)] = (mol dm⁻³)⁻¹ = dm³ mol⁻¹.

questions.question: What is the unit of Kc for 2NH₃ ⇌ N₂ + 3H₂?
questions.explanation: Kc = [N₂][H₂]³ / [NH₃]² has units (mol dm⁻³)⁴ / (mol dm⁻³)² = (mol dm⁻³)² = mol² dm⁻⁶.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes Qc from Kc?
options: Qc uses only product concentrations, while Kc uses only reactant concentrations
Qc is always equal to Kc
Kc changes during the reaction, while Qc stays fixed
Qc has the same form as Kc but uses concentrations at any instant, whereas Kc uses equilibrium concentrations
questions.explanation: Qc can be calculated at any time. Only when the mixture reaches equilibrium does Qc become equal to Kc.

questions.question: Separate closed vessels at the same temperature contain (i) H₂ and I₂, and (ii) the equivalent amount of HI alone. Both eventually reach the same equilibrium mixture. This shows that:
options: Equilibrium can be approached from either direction
Only the forward reaction takes place
Equilibrium can be reached only from the reactant side
questions.explanation: A true reversible reaction reaches the same equilibrium state whether you start from the reactants or from the products.

questions.question: For 2HI ⇌ H₂ + I₂, Kc = 0.04 at a certain temperature. If [HI] = 0.5 mol dm⁻³ at equilibrium and [H₂] = [I₂], what is [H₂]?
questions.explanation: [H₂][I₂] = Kc × [HI]² = 0.04 × 0.25 = 0.01. Since [H₂] = [I₂], [H₂]² = 0.01, so [H₂] = 0.1 mol dm⁻³.

questions.question: All species are gases in 4NH₃ + 5O₂ ⇌ 4NO + 6H₂O. What is the correct expression for Kc?
questions.explanation: Products NO (coefficient 4) and H₂O (coefficient 6) form the numerator; reactants NH₃ (4) and O₂ (5) form the denominator, each raised to its coefficient.
